summary:
The Investing in All of America Act of 2025 amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to revise the treatment of private capital and outstanding leverage for small business investment companies (SBICs), principally by expanding and modifying exclusions from SBIC maximum leverage calculations for specified investments.

Section 2(a) amends the definition of “private capital” in section 103(9) of the Small Business Investment Act of 1958, 15 U.S.C. 662(9). It removes the requirement in subparagraph (B)(iii)(I) that certain referenced plans have been “established prior to October 1, 1987,” and expands subparagraph (B)(iii)(II) to include funds from a “foundation, endowment, or trust of any college or university” in addition to a pension plan. It also adds a new subparagraph (C) providing that, for purposes of approval by the Administrator of a request for leverage, “private capital” does not include funds obtained directly or indirectly from any Federal, State, or local government, or any government agency or instrumentality, except for funds described in subparagraph (B)(iii)(I)–(III).

Section 2(b) amends section 303(b)(2) of the Act, 15 U.S.C. 683(b)(2), governing maximum leverage. It reduces the percentage limitation in subparagraph (A)(i) from 300 percent to 200 percent. It revises the per-company dollar cap in subparagraph (A)(ii) to $250,000,000 for a company making quarterly or semiannual interest payments, and $175,000,000 for any other company licensed under section 301(c). It revises the aggregate cap for commonly controlled licensees in subparagraph (B) to $475,000,000 for commonly controlled companies making quarterly or semiannual interest payments, and $350,000,000 for other commonly controlled section 301(c) licensees.

Section 2(b)(3) amends section 303(b)(2)(C) to broaden the leverage exclusion. As amended, investments by a company or commonly controlled companies may be excluded from outstanding leverage calculations under subparagraphs (A) and (B) if made in: a small business concern located in a low-income geographic area as defined in section 351 of the Act or a rural area as defined in 7 U.S.C. 1991(a)(13); a small business concern operating primarily in a covered technology category as defined in 10 U.S.C. 149(e); or a small manufacturer as defined in section 501(e)(6) of the Act. The exclusion is limited to the lesser of 50 percent of private capital or $125,000,000, must maintain the subparagraph (A)(i) limitation, and must be consistent with a leverage determination ratio issued under section 301(c). The exclusion applies only to investments made after enactment.
